newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Dec grain intervention offers to remain low.
newsitem.headline: German Dec grain intervention offers to remain low.

text.p: Sales offers into German grain intervention stores in the November-May 1996/97 season should remain low for the rest of December, an official at the state grain intervention board BLE said on Monday.
"We don't expect any significant volumes to be offered before the new year," a BLE official said, citing free market demand.
Volumes on November 29 totalled 230,603 tonnes compared with 956,859 tonnes a year earlier.
The figure comprised volumes accepted, but not yet delivered to stores, by the close last Friday.
Traders said market prices of grain in most regions were above intervention buying-in levels as feed grain demand outweighed sluggish milling industry demand.
July-August grain use in mixed feed output rose by 15 percent to 1.7 million tonnes over the same period last year, official figures showed.
Mixed feed output itself rose four percent to 4.59 million tonnes.

Positive signals from Brussels encouraged bread wheat and rye exporters' hopes of placing grain in third country markets. The latest intervention barley and rye export approvals also helped underpin the market.
Feed grain prices reversed some of the losses made in recent weeks as weather damage to the late maize harvest signalled some harvest reductions.
